For $f:X\to Y$ in this category, choose a *compactification* $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{\bar f}Y$, with $j$ an open immersion and $\bar f$ proper. (with rational bridge as explicitly defined above).

Representability and corepresentability must use the appropriate covariant or contravariant Hom variance. Finite-dimensional Hom spaces allow bidual identification and construction of a quasi-inverse.

theorem.title: Lemma — Serre functor exists

conclusions: For every integer n, the cohomology H^n(RHom(N,M)) agrees with Ext^n in D(B) from N to M; this is natural in M and contravariantly in N.
hypotheses: R is a commutative ring; A and B are dg R-algebras; N is a dg (A,B)-bimodule and M a dg right B-module.
theorem.statement:
Convention: a ring is commutative with $1$; an $R$-algebra is associative, unital and central over $R$.

Here $M$ is any differential graded right $B$-module, viewed as an object of $D(B,\mathrm d)$ as appropriate.

Let $(A, \text{d})$ and $(B, \text{d})$ be differential graded algebras
over a ring $R$. Let $N$ be a differential graded $(A, B)$-bimodule.
Then for every $n \in \mathbf{Z}$ there are isomorphisms
$$
H^n(R\Hom(N, M)) = \Ext^n_{D(B, \text{d})}(N, M)
$$
of $R$-modules functorial in $M$. It is also functorial in $N$
contravariantly under homomorphisms of differential graded $(A,B)$-bimodules (by precomposition on derived Hom).

theorem.statement:
Fix a base scheme $S$ and the big fppf site $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{\mathrm{fppf}}$. A category fibred in groupoids over this site assigns a groupoid of objects over each $S$-scheme, with pullback functors and coherent comparison isomorphisms. A stack in groupoids additionally satisfies effective descent for objects and the sheaf condition for isomorphisms under fppf covers. A representable fibred groupoid is the one associated to an algebraic space. All fibre products of such fibred groupoids are $2$-fibre products (objects include comparison isomorphisms).

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of fibred groupoids is representable by algebraic spaces if, for every scheme $T$ and $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$, the $2$-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is represented by an algebraic space $X_y$ over $T$. A representable morphism has a property such as étale, smooth, flat, locally of finite presentation, or surjective when every such $X_y\to T$ has that property. The diagonal $\Delta_\mathcal X:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times\mathcal X$ sends $x$ to $(x,x)$; its diagonal $\Delta_\Delta$ maps $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal X\times\mathcal X}\mathcal X$ and corresponds to the identity automorphism in the inertia groupoid. An algebraic stack is an fppf stack in groupoids with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective atlas by a scheme.

Let $\mathcal{X}$ be a category fibred in groupoids over $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\Delta_\Delta : \mathcal{X} \to
\mathcal{X} \times_{\mathcal{X} \times \mathcal{X}} \mathcal{X}$
is representable by algebraic spaces,
\item for every $1$-morphism $\mathcal{V} \to \mathcal{X} \times \mathcal{X}$
with $\mathcal{V}$ representable (by a scheme) the fibre product
$\mathcal{Y} =
\mathcal{X} \times_{\Delta, \mathcal{X} \times \mathcal{X}} \mathcal{V}$
has diagonal representable by algebraic spaces.
\end{enumerate}

For finite-length $R$-module $M$ and endomorphisms $\varphi,\psi:M\to M$ with $\varphi\psi=\psi\varphi=0$ and $\ker\varphi=\operatorname{im}\psi$, $\ker\psi=\operatorname{im}\varphi$, call $(M,\varphi,\psi)$ an exact $(2,1)$-periodic complex. With $I_\varphi=\operatorname{im}\varphi$, $I_\psi=\operatorname{im}\psi$, put $K_\varphi=\ker\varphi=I_\psi$, $K_\psi=\ker\psi=I_\varphi$. Let $\gamma_\varphi:\det K_\varphi\otimes\det I_\varphi\to\det M$, $\gamma_\psi:\det K_\psi\otimes\det I_\psi\to\det M$ be the determinant isomorphisms and $\sigma$ swap the tensor factors. Define $\det_\kappa(M,\varphi,\psi)\in\kappa^\times$ as the unique scalar such that $\gamma_\psi\circ\sigma\circ\gamma_\varphi^{-1}$ acts on $\det M$ by $(-1)^{\ell(I_\varphi)\ell(I_\psi)}\det_\kappa(M,\varphi,\psi)$.

conclusions: The Gysin pushforward satisfies the projection formula for the restriction $i^*\alpha$.

theorem.statement:
Let $X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes and $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a finitely presented closed immersion whose conormal sheaf $\mathcal C_{Z/X}=\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$ is locally free of constant rank $c\geq0$. Write $\mathcal H^c_Z(-)$ for the $c$th local cohomology sheaf supported on $Z$. Locally where $Z$ is defined by $c$ functions $f_1,\ldots,f_c$, the Gysin morphism $\gamma^p:\Omega^p_{Z/S}\to\mathcal H^c_Z(\Omega^{p+c}_{X/S})$ is given by a Čech/local-cohomology class represented by $\widetilde\omega\wedge df_1\wedge\cdots\wedge df_c/(f_1\cdots f_c)$ for a local lift $\widetilde\omega$ of $\omega$.
Assume $X\to S$ is smooth and $Z\hookrightarrow X$ is Koszul regular. Let $\gamma^{p,q}:H^q(Z,\Omega^p_{Z/S})\to H^{q+c}(X,\Omega^{p+c}_{X/S})$ be the Gysin map constructed from $\gamma^p$ and the map from cohomology with support to ordinary cohomology. Then for $\alpha\in H^q(X,\Omega^p_{X/S})$,
$$\gamma^{p,q}(i^*\alpha)=\alpha\cup\gamma^{0,0}(1)\quad\text{in }H^{q+c}(X,\Omega^{p+c}_{X/S}),$$
where $1\in H^0(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$.

theorem.title: Lemma — Effective support closed

conclusions: For every $A$-module $M$, $M^\vee$ is pure injective.
An $A$-module $I$ is pure injective if and only if the natural evaluation morphism $I\to (I^\vee)^\vee$ admits an $A$-linear retraction.
For every $A$-module $M$, there exists a universally exact sequence $0\to M\to I\to N\to0$ with $I$ pure injective.
hypotheses: Let $A$ be a ring; for an $A$-module $M$ write $M^\vee=\Hom_{\mathbf Z}(M,\mathbf Q/\mathbf Z)$, with its induced $A$-module structure.
theorem.statement:
Pinned-source conventions: a short exact sequence of $A$-modules is universally exact (pure exact) when it remains exact after tensoring with any $A$-module. An $A$-module $P$ is pure projective if $\Hom_A(P,-)$ takes every universally exact short exact sequence to a short exact sequence. An $A$-module $I$ is pure injective if $\Hom_A(-,I)$ takes every universally exact short exact sequence to a short exact sequence (with arrows reversed).

Let $A$ be a ring. For any $A$-module $M$ set
$M^\vee = \Hom_\mathbf{Z}(M, \mathbf{Q}/\mathbf{Z})$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For any $A$-module $M$ the $A$-module $M^\vee$ is pure injective.
\item An $A$-module $I$ is pure injective if and only if the map
$I \to (I^\vee)^\vee$ splits.
\item For any module $M$ there exists a universally exact sequence
$0 \to M \to I \to N \to 0$ with $I$ pure injective.
\end{enumerate}

theorem.statement:
For functions $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ on a ringed space, regular means successive multiplication maps on $\mathcal O/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})$ are injective; no nonzero-final-quotient condition is imposed here. Koszul-regular means the Koszul complex has zero homology in every positive degree; $H_1$-regular means its degree-one homology vanishes; quasi-regular means, with $\mathcal J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ the ideal sheaf generated by the sequence, that $(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal J^n/\mathcal J^{n+1}$ is an isomorphism, sending $T_i$ to $f_i$ modulo $\mathcal J^2$. An ideal sheaf is of a given type if near each point of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)$ it admits generators of that type. For a ring regular sequence one additionally requires the final quotient nonzero. An immersion is of a given type when its defining ideal on an open where it is closed is of that type. Relative quasi/$H_1$-regular means also that its source is flat over the base. Let $X$ be a locally ringed space. Let $\mathcal{J} \subset \mathcal{O}_X$
be a sheaf of ideals. Then $\mathcal{J}$ is quasi-regular if and
only if the following conditions are satisfied:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{J}$ is an $\mathcal{O}_X$-module of finite type,
\item $\mathcal{J}/\mathcal{J}^2$ is a finite locally free
$\mathcal{O}_X/\mathcal{J}$-module, and
\item the canonical maps
$$
\text{Sym}^n_{\mathcal{O}_X/\mathcal{J}}(\mathcal{J}/\mathcal{J}^2)
\longrightarrow
\mathcal{J}^n/\mathcal{J}^{n + 1}
$$
are isomorphisms for all $n \geq 0$.
\end{enumerate}

theorem.title: Lemma — Formal consequence

conclusions: i is quasi-regular iff it is locally of finite presentation, its conormal sheaf is finite locally free, and $\operatorname{Sym}^*(\mathcal C_{Z/X})\to\mathcal C_{Z/X,*}$ is an isomorphism.
hypotheses: $i:Z\to X$ is an immersion of schemes.
theorem.statement:
For functions $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ on a ringed space, regular means successive multiplication maps on $\mathcal O/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})$ are injective; no nonzero-final-quotient condition is imposed here. Koszul-regular means the Koszul complex has zero homology in every positive degree; $H_1$-regular means its degree-one homology vanishes; quasi-regular means, with $\mathcal J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ the ideal sheaf generated by the sequence, that $(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal J^n/\mathcal J^{n+1}$ is an isomorphism, sending $T_i$ to $f_i$ modulo $\mathcal J^2$. An ideal sheaf is of a given type if near each point of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)$ it admits generators of that type. For a ring regular sequence one additionally requires the final quotient nonzero. An immersion is of a given type when its defining ideal on an open where it is closed is of that type. Relative quasi/$H_1$-regular means also that its source is flat over the base. For an immersion $i:Z\to X$, choose an open $V\subset X$ where it is closed, with ideal $\mathcal I$; the conormal algebra $\mathcal C_{Z/X,*}$ has degree $n$ piece corresponding to $\mathcal I^n/\mathcal I^{n+1}$ on $Z$, and $\mathcal C_{Z/X}=\mathcal C_{Z/X,1}$. Its canonical map from $\operatorname{Sym}^*(\mathcal C_{Z/X})$ is induced by multiplication of ideals. Let $i : Z \to X$ be an immersion of schemes. Then $i$ is a quasi-regular
immersion if and only if the following conditions are satisfied
\begin{enumerate}
\item $i$ is locally of finite presentation,
\item the conormal sheaf $\mathcal{C}_{Z/X}$ is finite locally free, and
\item the map (\ref{equation-conormal-algebra-quotient}) is an isomorphism.
\end{enumerate}

theorem.title: Lemma — Descent representable transformations property

conclusions: Bifunctorial pro-adjunction Hom(K,f^!L)≈Hom_Pro(Rf_!K,L).
hypotheses: f in FTS_S, K bounded coherent on X, L bounded below coherent on Y, compactification-based upper/lower shriek.
theorem.statement:
Fix a Noetherian base scheme $S$; let $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ be the category of separated schemes of finite type over $S$. For $f:X\to Y$ in this category, the *upper shriek* $f^!$ sends $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)$ to $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ and is built from proper compactification $X\hookrightarrow\bar X\xrightarrow{\bar f}Y$ by $j^*a_{\bar f}$, where $a_{\bar f}$ is right adjoint to $R\bar f_*$. The corresponding *lower shriek* $Rf_!:D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_X)\to\operatorname{Pro}(D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_Y))$ is $R\bar f_*Rj_!$ for any compactification; proper pushforward is applied termwise to the pro-system. Then for every $K\in D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_X)$ and every *bounded-below coherent* $L\in D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)$ there is a bifunctorial isomorphism of Hom sets
\[
\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X)}(K,f^!L)
\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Pro}(D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y))}(Rf_!K,L).
\]
The right side regards $L$ as a **constant** pro-object; this is the coherent pro-category analogue of an adjunction, not an ordinary adjunction between $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(X)$ and $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^+(Y)$ alone.

theorem.statement: For a Noetherian ring $A$, let $D_{\rm Coh}(A)\subseteq D(A)$ be the full derived category of complexes with finitely generated cohomology in every degree. A *dualizing complex* $\omega_A^\bullet\in D(A)$ means a bounded complex with finite injective dimension and finitely generated cohomology such that the homothety map $A\to R\operatorname{Hom}_A(\omega_A^\bullet,\omega_A^\bullet)$ is an isomorphism. No cohomological shift is needed merely to obtain *a* dualizing complex; normalization in a local sense is a separate question.

theorem.title: Lemma — Syntomic locally finite presentation

conclusions: Difference of dimension functions equals transcendence degree of residue field.
hypotheses: Finite type X/S, dualizing D_X normalized relative D_S, dimension function by normalized stalk.
theorem.statement:
Fix a Noetherian scheme $S$ and a dualizing complex $D_S\in D(\mathcal O_S)$. For a finite-type $S$-scheme $T$, choose a finite open covering $\mathcal U=\{U_i\}$ by $S$-separated schemes, and let $p_i:U_i\to S$. Define $D_i=p_i^!D_S$, using the upper-shriek functors of separated finite-type schemes over $S$. On overlaps $U_{ij}$ their restrictions have canonical comparison isomorphisms $\varphi_{ij}:D_i|_{U_{ij}}\xrightarrow{\sim}D_j|_{U_{ij}}$ satisfying the cocycle condition on triple overlaps. A *dualizing complex normalized relative to $D_S$ and $\mathcal U$* is a pair $(D_T,\{\alpha_i\})$ with $D_T\in D(\mathcal O_T)$ and compatible isomorphisms $\alpha_i:D_T|_{U_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}D_i$, such that $\alpha_j\alpha_i^{-1}=\varphi_{ij}$ on each overlap. The normalized object includes the local identifications, not merely the derived isomorphism class of $D_T$. For a dualizing complex $D_T$ on a locally Noetherian scheme $T$, its associated dimension function $\delta_T:T\to\mathbf Z$ assigns to $t$ the unique integer such that the stalk $D_{T,t}[-\delta_T(t)]$ is a *normalized* dualizing complex over $\mathcal O_{T,t}$, i.e. $R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{T,t}}(\kappa(t),D_{T,t}[-\delta_T(t)])\simeq\kappa(t)[0]$. For $x\in X$ above $y\in Y$, let $X_y=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ be the fibre and $\dim_x(X_y)$ its local topological dimension at $x$ (minimum dimension of neighbourhoods in the fibre). Let $f:X\to S$ be of finite type, and $D_X$ normalized relative to $D_S$. For every $x\in X$, with $s=f(x)$, one has
\[
\delta_X(x)-\delta_S(s)=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(x).
\]
Here $\delta_X,\delta_S$ are normalized dualizing dimension functions, and $\kappa(x)/\kappa(s)$ is the induced residue-field extension.

A category fibred in groupoids over this site assigns a groupoid of objects over each $S$-scheme, with pullback functors and coherent comparison isomorphisms. A stack in groupoids additionally satisfies effective descent for objects and the sheaf condition for isomorphisms under fppf covers. A representable fibred groupoid is the one associated to an algebraic space. All fibre products of such fibred groupoids are $2$-fibre products (objects include comparison isomorphisms).

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of fibred groupoids is representable by algebraic spaces if, for every scheme $T$ and $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$, the $2$-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is represented by an algebraic space $X_y$ over $T$. A representable morphism has a property such as étale, smooth, flat, locally of finite presentation, or surjective when every such $X_y\to T$ has that property. The diagonal $\Delta_\mathcal X:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times\mathcal X$ sends $x$ to $(x,x)$; its diagonal $\Delta_\Delta$ maps $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal X\times\mathcal X}\mathcal X$ and corresponds to the identity automorphism in the inertia groupoid. An algebraic stack is an fppf stack in groupoids with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective atlas by a scheme.

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ is limit preserving on objects if, whenever an affine scheme $U=\varprojlim_i U_i$ is an inverse limit of affine $S$-schemes, $y_i\in\mathcal Y(U_i)$, $x\in\mathcal X(U)$, and an isomorphism $\gamma:p(x)\xrightarrow{\sim}y_i|_U$ are given, then for some $j\ge i$ there exist $x_j\in\mathcal X(U_j)$, an isomorphism $\beta:x_j|_U\xrightarrow{\sim}x$, and an isomorphism $\gamma_j:p(x_j)\xrightarrow{\sim}y_i|_{U_j}$ whose pullback to $U$ agrees with $\gamma$ after $p(\beta)$.

A representable fibred groupoid is the one associated to an algebraic space. All fibre products of such fibred groupoids are $2$-fibre products (objects include comparison isomorphisms).

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of fibred groupoids is representable by algebraic spaces if, for every scheme $T$ and $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$, the $2$-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is represented by an algebraic space $X_y$ over $T$. A representable morphism has a property such as étale, smooth, flat, locally of finite presentation, or surjective when every such $X_y\to T$ has that property. The diagonal $\Delta_\mathcal X:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times\mathcal X$ sends $x$ to $(x,x)$; its diagonal $\Delta_\Delta$ maps $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal X\times\mathcal X}\mathcal X$ and corresponds to the identity automorphism in the inertia groupoid. An algebraic stack is an fppf stack in groupoids with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective atlas by a scheme.

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ is limit preserving on objects if, whenever an affine scheme $U=\varprojlim_i U_i$ is an inverse limit of affine $S$-schemes, $y_i\in\mathcal Y(U_i)$, $x\in\mathcal X(U)$, and an isomorphism $\gamma:p(x)\xrightarrow{\sim}y_i|_U$ are given, then for some $j\ge i$ there exist $x_j\in\mathcal X(U_j)$, an isomorphism $\beta:x_j|_U\xrightarrow{\sim}x$, and an isomorphism $\gamma_j:p(x_j)\xrightarrow{\sim}y_i|_{U_j}$ whose pullback to $U$ agrees with $\gamma$ after $p(\beta)$.

Let $p : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Y}$ and $q : \mathcal{Y} \to \mathcal{Z}$
be $1$-morphisms of categories fibred in groupoids over $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$.
If $p$ and $q$ are limit preserving on objects, then so is the composition
$q \circ p$.

conclusions:
\begin{reference}
Variant of \cite[Lemma 2.15]{Orlov-K3}
\end{reference}
Let $F : \mathcal{D} \to \mathcal{D}'$ be an exact functor of
triangulated categories. Let $S \subset \Ob(\mathcal{D})$ be
a set of objects. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $F$ has both right and left adjoints,
\item for $K \in \mathcal{D}$ if $\Hom(E, K[i]) = 0$ for all
$E \in S$ and $i \in \mathbf{Z}$ then $K = 0$,
\item for $K \in \mathcal{D}$ if $\Hom(K, E[i]) = 0$ for all
$E \in S$ and $i \in \mathbf{Z}$ then $K = 0$,
\item the map $\Hom(E, E'[i]) \to \Hom(F(E), F(E')[i])$ induced by $F$
is bijective for all $E, E' \in S$ and $i \in \mathbf{Z}$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $F$ is fully faithful.
S is a set of left- and right-spanning objects: vanishing of all shifted Hom from S and to S separately detects zero. Both adjoints to F are assumed, and the Hom comparison for all E,E' in S and all shifts is bijective.

hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field. A proper curve over $k$ is a proper integral $k$-scheme of Krull dimension one; a proper $k$-scheme of dimension one need not be integral. For any proper such scheme $X$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, define its genus as $g(X)=\dim_k H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is one-dimensional, Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional, its coherent dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is invertible when $X$ is Gorenstein.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$, $\operatorname{Pic}(X)$ is the group of isomorphism classes of invertible $\mathcal O_X$-modules, and $\operatorname{Pic}(X)[n]=\{\mathcal L:\mathcal L^{\otimes n}\cong\mathcal O_X\}$. If $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$ and $\dim X=1$, the arithmetic genus is $g=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. theorem.title: Lemma — Local cohomology and restriction

conclusions: For every U∈B, j_{U!}O_U has the **bounded-below** compactness property: Hom(j_{U!}O_U,⊕_iM_i)≅⊕_iHom(j_{U!}O_U,M_i) whenever the sum is bounded below.
hypotheses: (C,O) is a ringed site, B⊂Ob(C), and Cov is a selection of its covering families.
Every cover in Cov is finite, its target/members and all iterated fibre products lie in B.
For each U∈B, the selected Cov-covers of U are cofinal among all coverings of U.
theorem.statement:
In a triangulated derived category D(A), a **compact object** K is one for which Hom(K,⊕_i M_i)≅⊕_iHom(K,M_i) for **arbitrary** families. A distinct bounded-below-only compactness property is used in D^+(O): it is tested only on direct sums M=⊕ M_i that are bounded below as a whole. For a site object U, j_{U!}O_U is extension by zero from the ringed slice, and its representability relates Hom to derived sections over U. The selected covers Cov form a **finite cofinal system** for every U∈B, with all finite iterated fibre products remaining in B; this condition, not mere quasi-compactness of U, is the source hypothesis.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site
with set of coverings $\text{Cov}_\mathcal{C}$.
Let $\mathcal{B} \subset \Ob(\mathcal{C})$, and
$\text{Cov} \subset \text{Cov}_\mathcal{C}$
be subsets. Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every $\mathcal{U} \in \text{Cov}$ we have
$\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$ with $I$ finite,
$U, U_i \in \mathcal{B}$ and every
$U_{i_0} \times_U \ldots \times_U U_{i_p} \in \mathcal{B}$.
\item For every $U \in \mathcal{B}$ the coverings of $U$
occurring in $\text{Cov}$ is a cofinal system of coverings of $U$.
\end{enumerate}
Then for $U \in \mathcal{B}$ the object $j_{U!}\mathcal{O}_U$ is
a compact object of $D^+(\mathcal{O})$ in the following sense:
if $M = \bigoplus_{i \in I} M_i$ in $D(\mathcal{O})$ is
bounded below, then $\Hom(j_{U!}\mathcal{O}_U, M) =
\bigoplus_{i \in I} \Hom(j_{U!}\mathcal{O}_U, M_i)$.

$\tau \in \{Zariski, \etale, smooth, syntomic, fppf\}$.

\begin{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}

$U_i/X$ is an object of $\mathcal{C}_t$,
\item $U \times \mathbf{A}^1/X$ is an object of $\mathcal{C}_t$.
\end{enumerate}
\item $X/X$ is an object of $\mathcal{C}_t$.
\end{enumerate}
We endow $\mathcal{C}_t$ with the structure of a site whose coverings are
exactly those coverings $\{U_i \to U\}$ of $(\Sch/X)_\tau$ with
$U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C}_t)$. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] The functor $\mathcal{C}_1 \to \mathcal{C}_2$
is fully faithful, continuous, and cocontinuous.
\end{enumerate}
Denote $g : \Sh(\mathcal{C}_1) \to \Sh(\mathcal{C}_2)$ the corresponding
morphism of topoi. Denote $\mathcal{O}_t$ the restriction of $\mathcal{O}$
to $\mathcal{C}_t$. Denote $g_!$ the functor of
Modules on Sites, Definition \ref{sites-modules-definition-g-shriek}.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(b)] The canonical map $g_!\mathcal{O}_1 \to \mathcal{O}_2$
is an isomorphism.
\end{enumerate}
The sites are **full subcategories** of the selected big-$\tau$ site, closed under base-site covering members and $U\times_X\mathbf A^1_X$, containing $X/X$. The left adjoint $g_!$ here is the **module lower-shriek** functor from the included site, and the comparison is specifically $g_!\mathcal O_1\simeq\mathcal O_2$.

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

For a flat morphism $h:T'\to T$ of relative dimension $r$, the flat pullback $h^*:Z_q(T)\to Z_{q+r}(T')$ sends $[W]$ to the cycle $[T'\times_TW]_{q+r}$ weighted by the lengths at generic points of components. It descends to Chow groups.

For a closed immersion $j:Z\hookrightarrow X$, let $\mathcal C_{Z/X}=\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$ be its conormal sheaf. A virtual normal sheaf for $Z$ in $X$ consists of a finite locally free $\mathcal N$ on $Z$ and a specified surjection $\mathcal N^\vee\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal C_{Z/X}$. The induced closed immersion of the normal cone $C_ZX=\operatorname{Spec}_Z\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\mathcal I^n/\mathcal I^{n+1}$ into the vector bundle $\operatorname{Spec}_Z\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal N^\vee)$ defines the associated completed bivariant Gysin class $c(Z\to X,\mathcal N)\in A^*(Z\to X)^\wedge$ via deformation to the normal cone. If $\mathcal N$ has constant rank $r$, this class has degree $r$. Pullback of this class along a morphism over $X$ is denoted $\operatorname{res}$; $c_{\mathrm{top}}(\mathcal E)$ means $c_{\operatorname{rank}\mathcal E}(\mathcal E)$.

A regular immersion is a closed immersion whose defining ideal is locally generated by a regular sequence; its normal sheaf is the dual of the conormal sheaf and defines a bivariant Gysin class $i^!$. A local complete intersection (lci) morphism $f:X\to Y$ admits locally a factorization as a regular immersion followed by a smooth morphism. When a global factorization $f=g\circ i$ exists with $i:X\hookrightarrow P$ a regular immersion and $g:P\to Y$ smooth, define its Gysin class $f^!=i^!\circ g^*$; it is independent of the chosen factorization. Smooth pullback $g^*$ denotes the flat bivariant class with its dimension degree.

and for some $r$ we have ${}'E_r^{p, q} \in \mathcal{C}$ for all
$p, q \in \mathbf{Z}$, then $H^n(\text{Tot}(K^{\bullet, \bullet}))$
is in $\mathcal{C}$. Similarly for $({}''E_r, {}''d_r)_{r \geq 0}$.

theorem.statement: Fix a Noetherian base $S$. Write $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ for separated schemes of finite type over $S$, with $S$-morphisms. For $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$, choose a factorization $f=\bar f\circ j$ with $j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$ an open immersion and $\bar f:\bar X\to Y$ proper. Consider any cartesian square $X'=X\times_YY'$ with maps $f:X\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $g:Y'\to Y$, and $g':X'\to X$ in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$. Suppose $f$ is flat and $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)$ is such that $Lg^*E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_{Y'})$. theorem.statement:

Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$ be composable qcqs scheme maps, $h=g\circ f$, and write $a=a_f$, $b=a_g$, $c=a_h\simeq a\circ b$. For any $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$ there are two natural maps from
\[
Lf^*(Lg^*K\otimes_Y^{\mathbf L}b(\mathcal O_Z))\otimes_X^{\mathbf L}a(\mathcal O_Y)
\]
to $c(K)$: (i) apply $\mu_{f,Lg^*K\otimes b(\mathcal O_Z)}$ and then $a(\mu_{g,K})$, or (ii) first apply the base-change associativity and the comparison at the structure sheaf to identify the source with $Lh^*K\otimes_X^{\mathbf L}c(\mathcal O_Z)$, then apply $\mu_{h,K}$. theorem.title: Lemma — Thickening quasi affine

conclusions: Any algebraic space locally of finite type over $X$ is Jacobson.
hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

An algebraic space $X$ is decent if every point $x\in|X|$ admits a quasi-compact representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is reasonable if every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has universally bounded finite fibres, and very reasonable if it is Zariski-locally covered by quasi-compact surjective étale schemes. A morphism $f:X\to Y$ is *decent* (respectively reasonable, very reasonable or with property $(\beta)$) if $X\times_YT$ has that property for every scheme $T\to Y$. Property $(\beta)$ for a space means that every point can be represented by a monomorphism from a field spectrum.

For decent $X$ and $x\in|X|$, $\kappa(x)$ is the field associated with the representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. An *elementary étale neighborhood* $(U,u)\to(X,x)$ is an étale scheme chart whose pointed field map $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to X$ is such a monomorphism. Its henselian local ring is $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{h}=\varinjlim_{(U,u)}\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ over the cofiltered category of elementary étale neighborhoods, and it agrees with $\mathcal O_{U,u}^h$ for any one of them. A decent space's point-set $|X|$ is sober and admits a dense open schematic locus when it has finitely many irreducible components.

An algebraic space $X$ is *Jacobson* if it admits an étale surjective cover by Jacobson schemes. A topological space $|X|$ is Jacobson if closed points are dense in every closed subset. A *finite type point* $x\in X_{\mathrm{ft\text{-}pts}}$ is a point represented by a morphism from a field spectrum locally of finite type over $X$. A decent locally Noetherian algebraic space has a sober underlying topological space, and its specialization relations agree locally with those on elementary étale scheme charts.

For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. An algebraic space $X$ is decent if every point $x\in|X|$ admits a quasi-compact representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. For an inverse system of complexes $(K_n)$ in $D(\mathcal O)$, $R\varprojlim K_n$ is its homotopy/derived inverse limit. The $R^1\varprojlim$ terms are first right-derived inverse limits of systems of abelian groups, and the natural comparison to the termwise inverse limit need not be an isomorphism without additional hypotheses. elements of $\mathcal{B}$,

\begin{enumerate}
\item $H^p(U, H^q(K_n)) = 0$ for $p > 0$,
\item the inverse system $H^0(U, H^q(K_n))$ has vanishing $R^1\lim$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
Then $H^q(R\lim K_n) = \lim H^q(K_n)$ for $q \in \mathbf{Z}$.

theorem.title: Lemma — Classical generator generator

conclusions: Derived dual with ω_A equals degree-zero Matlis dual.
hypotheses: Normalized local dualizing ω_A, injective hull E, finite-length N.
theorem.statement:
Let $(A,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ be a Noetherian local ring, with a *normalized* dualizing complex $\omega_A^\bullet$: this is a dualizing complex satisfying $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(\kappa,\omega_A^\bullet)\simeq\kappa[0]$. For an $A$-module $M$ put $\operatorname{Ext}_A^i(M,\omega_A^\bullet)=H^i(R\operatorname{Hom}_A(M,\omega_A^\bullet))$. Let $E$ be an injective hull of the residue field $\kappa$, i.e. an injective $A$-module in which $\kappa$ is an essential submodule. For every finite-length $A$-module $N$, there is a natural isomorphism in $D(A)$
\[
R\operatorname{Hom}_A(N,\omega_A^\bullet)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_A(N,E)[0].
\]
The right-hand side is the ordinary Matlis dual viewed in degree $0$; its derived higher cohomology vanishes on finite-length $N$. The isomorphism is functorial in $N$, not merely one selected for each module.

theorem.title: Lemma — Finite type local source fppf algebra

conclusions: Projection-comparison map is an isomorphism for every K in unbounded D_QCoh.
hypotheses: f proper flat finite presentation over qcqs Y.
theorem.statement:
Let $Y$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated and $f:X\to Y$ proper, flat, and of finite presentation. Let $a_f$ be the right adjoint to $Rf_*$ on unbounded derived categories with quasi-coherent cohomology, and define the *relative dualizing complex* $\omega_{X/Y}^{\bullet}=a_f(\mathcal O_Y)\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$. For a qcqs morphism $f:X\to Y$ with right adjoint $a_f$, let $\mu_{f,K}:Lf^*K\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}^{\mathbf L}a_f(\mathcal O_Y)\to a_f(K)$ be the canonical comparison obtained by adjunction from the projection formula $Rf_*(Lf^*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}a_f(\mathcal O_Y))\simeq K\otimes^{\mathbf L}Rf_*a_f(\mathcal O_Y)$ followed by the counit $Rf_*a_f(\mathcal O_Y)\to\mathcal O_Y$. For every (possibly unbounded) $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ the canonical morphism
\[
Lf^*K\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}^{\mathbf L}\omega_{X/Y}^{\bullet}\xrightarrow{\mu_{f,K}}a_f(K)
\]
is an isomorphism. In particular, the functor $a_f$ is obtained by derived pullback followed by tensoring with the relative dualizing complex, functorially on the full unbounded quasi-coherent derived category.

theorem.statement:
Let $\varphi:R\to A$ be a finite-type homomorphism of Noetherian rings. Define its *algebraic upper-shriek functor* $\varphi^!:D(R)\to D(A)$ by choosing a presentation $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow A$ and putting
\[

\]
For surjective $\varphi$, one may use $\varphi^!(K)=R\operatorname{Hom}_R(A,K)$ with its natural $A$-action. Different polynomial presentations give isomorphic functors, but the isomorphisms are *not canonical*. Here $D^\pm$ means bounded below/above cohomology, $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}$ means coherent cohomology, and a *perfect* ring map is pseudo-coherent and of finite Tor dimension (equivalently $A$ is a perfect $P$-complex after a suitable finite polynomial presentation).

Let $\varphi : A \to B$ be a finite type homomorphism of Noetherian rings.
Let $\omega_A^\bullet$ be a dualizing complex for $A$. Set
$\omega_B^\bullet = \varphi^!(\omega_A^\bullet)$. Denote
$D_A(K) = R\Hom_A(K, \omega_A^\bullet)$ for $K \in D_{\textit{Coh}}(A)$
and
$D_B(L) = R\Hom_B(L, \omega_B^\bullet)$ for $L \in D_{\textit{Coh}}(B)$.
Then there is a functorial isomorphism
$$
\varphi^!(K) = D_B(D_A(K) \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} B)
$$
for $K \in D_{\textit{Coh}}(A)$.

D_A and D_B are two different ring-specific duality functors: D_A(K)=RHom_A(K,ω_A) and D_B(L)=RHom_B(L,ω_B), ω_B=φ^!(ω_A).

theorem.title: Lemma — Choices

conclusions: Every quasi-coherent descent datum is effective, and restriction to the covering is fully faithful.
hypotheses: $S$ is affine and $\mathcal U$ is a finite standard fpqc family of affine schemes with faithfully flat disjoint union over $S$.
theorem.statement: Let $S=\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ be affine, and let $\mathcal U=\{f_i:U_i\to S\}_{i=1}^n$ be a finite standard fpqc covering: each $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}(A_i)$ is affine, and the map $\coprod_{i=1}^nU_i\to S$ is faithfully flat (equivalently, $R\to\prod_{i=1}^nA_i$ is faithfully flat). Given a family of scheme maps $\{U_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$, a descent datum for quasi-coherent sheaves is a collection of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{U_i}$-modules $\mathcal F_i$ with isomorphisms $\phi_{ij}:\operatorname{pr}_0^*\mathcal F_i\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{pr}_1^*\mathcal F_j$ on $U_i\times_S U_j$ satisfying the cocycle condition on every triple overlap. It is effective if the $\mathcal F_i$ are obtained, up to isomorphism of descent data, by pullback of a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module. Then every such datum is effective and the canonical functor $\operatorname{QCoh}(S)\to\operatorname{Desc}_{\mathcal U}(\operatorname{QCoh})$ is fully faithful; in fact it is an equivalence.

hypotheses: Let $(K^\bullet,F)$ be a filtered complex in an abelian category with countable direct sums.
theorem.statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $(K^\bullet, F)$ be a filtered complex of $\mathcal{A}$.
Assume $\mathcal{A}$ has countable direct sums.
Let $(E_r, d_r)_{r \geq 0}$ be the spectral sequence
associated to $(K^\bullet, F)$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The map
$$
d_1^{p, q} :
E_1^{p, q} = H^{p + q}(\text{gr}^p(K^\bullet))
\longrightarrow
E_1^{p + 1, q} = H^{p + q + 1}(\text{gr}^{p + 1}(K^\bullet))
$$
is equal to the boundary map in cohomology associated to the short
exact sequence of complexes
$$
0 \to \text{gr}^{p + 1}(K^\bullet) \to
F^pK^\bullet/F^{p + 2}K^\bullet \to \text{gr}^p(K^\bullet) \to 0.
$$
\item Assume that $d(F^pK) \subset F^{p + 1}K$ for all $p \in \mathbf{Z}$.
Then $d$ induces the zero differential on $\text{gr}^p(K^\bullet)$
and hence
$E_1^{p, q} = \text{gr}^p(K^\bullet)^{p + q}$.
Furthermore, in this case
$$
d_1^{p, q} :
E_1^{p, q} = \text{gr}^p(K^\bullet)^{p + q}
\longrightarrow
E_1^{p + 1, q} = \text{gr}^{p + 1}(K^\bullet)^{p + q + 1}
$$
is the morphism induced by $d$.
\end{enumerate}

conclusions: The property "Jacobson" holds on S exactly when it holds on all covering schemes S_i.

theorem.title: Lemma — Morphism sheaves with P effective descent etale

conclusions: Associated-sheaf equivalences commute with pullback; generally not with big-site pushforward; qcqs small-Zariski/étale pushforward is compatible.
hypotheses: f:T→S is a scheme morphism; qcqs is required for the small-site pushforward claim.
theorem.statement:
For $\tau$ among Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, and fppf, let $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_\tau$ be the big site of all schemes over $S$ with the stated topology and structure sheaf $\mathcal O(T\to S)=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$. The small Zariski site $S_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ and small étale site $S_{\mathrm{\acute et}}$ have as objects open immersions or étale morphisms to $S$, respectively, with the corresponding structure sheaf.
For a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module $\mathcal F$, denote by $\mathcal F^a$ the $\mathcal O$-module on the indicated site given on each object $g:T\to S$ by $\mathcal F^a(T)=\Gamma(T,g^*\mathcal F)$ (restricted to the small site when appropriate). Let $f:T\to S$ be a morphism of schemes. (1) For every eligible $\tau$, passing from quasi-coherent sheaves to the associated big-site sheaves commutes with pullback, and the same holds on the small Zariski and étale sites: $f_{\mathrm{site}}^*(\mathcal G^a)\cong(f^*\mathcal G)^a$. (2) The analogous big-site pushforward compatibility is false in general (and $f_*$ need not preserve quasi-coherence). (3) If $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, then for $\tau\in\{\mathrm{Zariski},\mathrm{\acute etale}\}$ both $f_*$ on schemes and $f_{\mathrm{small},*}$ on small sites preserve quasi-coherent sheaves, and $f_{\mathrm{small},*}(\mathcal F^a)\cong(f_*\mathcal F)^a$ for every quasi-coherent $\mathcal F$ on $T$.

theorem.title: Lemma — Descending property surjective

conclusions: There is a functorial long exact cohomology sequence with degree-raising connecting maps, compatible with shifted cohomology $H^j(K[k])\cong H^{j+k}(K)$.
hypotheses: $0\to A^\bullet\to B^\bullet\to C^\bullet\to0$ is short exact in cochain complexes of an abelian category.
theorem.statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category. Suppose that
$$
0 \to
A^\bullet \to
B^\bullet \to
C^\bullet \to
0
$$
is a short exact sequence of cochain complexes of $\mathcal{A}$.
Then there is a long exact cohomology sequence
$$
\xymatrix{
\ldots & \ldots & \ldots \ar[lld] \\
H^i(A^\bullet) \ar[r] &
H^i(B^\bullet) \ar[r] &
H^i(C^\bullet) \ar[lld] \\
H^{i + 1}(A^\bullet) \ar[r] &
H^{i + 1}(B^\bullet) \ar[r] &
H^{i + 1}(C^\bullet) \ar[lld] \\
\ldots & \ldots & \ldots \\
}
$$
The construction produces long exact cohomology sequences
which are functorial in the short exact
sequence and compatible with shifts as in
the cochain-shift identification $H^j(K[k])\cong H^{j+k}(K)$ using the signed shift differential.

**Source-defined terminology (not inherited hypotheses):** A **w-local** spectral space has closed closed-point set and unique closed specialization of each point; a w-local map is spectral and maps closed points to closed points. An **ind-étale** map is a filtered colimit of étale algebras. A ring $A$ is **w-contractible** iff every faithfully flat weakly étale map $A\to B$ admits an $A$-algebra retraction.

Let $A$ be a ring. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A$ is w-contractible,
\item every faithfully flat, ind-\'etale ring map $A \to B$ has
a retraction, and
\item $A$ satisfies
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\Spec(A)$ is w-local,
\item $\pi_0(\Spec(A))$ is extremally disconnected, and
\item for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m \subset A$ the
local ring $A_\mathfrak m$ is strictly henselian.
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}

theorem.title: Lemma — W local strictly henselian extremally disconnected

conclusions: $L_{B/A}$ is a perfect complex with tor amplitude in $[-1, 0]$.
hypotheses: For a ring map $A\to B$, let $\Omega_{B/A}$ be the module of Kähler differentials. The cotangent complex $L_{B/A}\in D(B)$ is obtained from the standard augmented simplicial polynomial $A$-algebra resolution $P_\bullet\to B$, where $P_0=A[B]$, $P_1=A[A[B]]$, etc., by taking the chain complex (in nonpositive cohomological degrees) associated to the simplicial $B$-module $\Omega_{P_\bullet/A}\otimes_{P_\bullet}B$. Here $A[E]$ denotes the polynomial algebra freely generated by a set $E$, $D(B)$ is the derived category of $B$-modules, and $H^i$ denotes degree-$i$ cohomology.

A quasi-isomorphism is a map of complexes inducing an isomorphism on every cohomology module. We write $M[0]$ for a module concentrated in degree zero, $M[1]$ for a module in degree $-1$, $\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}$ for derived tensor product, and $\tau_{\geq -1}$ for the standard truncation in cohomological degrees at least $-1$. The module $\Omega_{B/A}$ is generated by symbols $db$ subject to additivity, the Leibniz rule, and $da=0$ for $a\in A$.

An ordered sequence $(f_1,\dots,f_r)$ in a ring $A$ is Koszul-regular if the Koszul complex $K(f_1,\dots,f_r;A)$ has no positive-degree homology. A Koszul ideal is locally generated by a Koszul-regular sequence. A local complete intersection (lci) ring map $A\to B$ locally factors as a smooth algebra map followed by a quotient whose kernel is generated by a regular sequence. For a ring map $A\to B$, let $\Omega_{B/A}$ be the module of Kähler differentials. The cotangent complex $L_{B/A}\in D(B)$ is obtained from the standard augmented simplicial polynomial $A$-algebra resolution $P_\bullet\to B$, where $P_0=A[B]$, $P_1=A[A[B]]$, etc., by taking the chain complex (in nonpositive cohomological degrees) associated to the simplicial $B$-module $\Omega_{P_\bullet/A}\otimes_{P_\bullet}B$. theorem.title: Lemma — Frobenius gives norm for reduction

conclusions: K^vee:=RSheafHom(K,O) is perfect and the double dual (K^vee)^vee≅K.
For every M there is a natural isomorphism M⊗^L_O K^vee≅RSheafHom(K,M).
The associated map H^0(C,M⊗^L_O K^vee)≅Hom_{D(O)}(K,M) is an isomorphism of groups.
hypotheses: (C,O) is a ringed site, K∈D(O) is perfect and M∈D(O).
theorem.statement:
For a ringed site (C,O), the monoidal category of complexes uses total tensor with signed differential, and the symmetric monoidal category D(O) uses derived tensor ⊗^L with Koszul signs. A *left dual* of K is an object K^vee with coevaluation η:O→K⊗K^vee and evaluation ε:K^vee⊗K→O satisfying both triangular identities (using the relevant underived or derived tensor). For perfect K, K^vee=RSheafHom(K,O), and for a chain complex locally strictly perfect the ordinary Hom complex supplies its candidate dual. For any **perfect derived** K, the derived dual K^vee:=RSheafHom(K,O) is again perfect; the formulas are functorial in every M∈D(O), and the H^0 equality is a group-level global-section equality.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $K$ be a perfect object of $D(\mathcal{O})$.
Then $K^\vee = R\SheafHom(K, \mathcal{O})$ is a
perfect object too and $(K^\vee)^\vee \cong K$. There are
functorial isomorphisms
$$
M \otimes^\mathbf{L}_\mathcal{O} K^\vee = R\SheafHom_\mathcal{O}(K, M)
$$
and
$$
H^0(\mathcal{C}, M \otimes^\mathbf{L}_\mathcal{O} K^\vee) =
\Hom_{D(\mathcal{O})}(K, M)
$$
for $M$ in $D(\mathcal{O})$.

theorem.title: Lemma — Isomorphism

$$

& &
(\Sh(\mathcal{D}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D}) \ar[d]^{(e, e^\sharp)}
\\
(\Sh(\mathcal{C}'), \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{C}'})
\ar[rr]^{(h, h^\sharp)} & &
(\Sh(\mathcal{D}'), \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{D}'})
}
$$
where
\begin{enumerate}
\item $g : \Sh(\mathcal{C}) \to \Sh(\mathcal{C}')$
is an equivalence of topoi induced by a special cocontinuous functor
$\mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{C}'$ (see

\item $e : \Sh(\mathcal{D}) \to \Sh(\mathcal{D}')$

and $g^\sharp$ is the obvious map,
\item $\mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{D}'} = e_*\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D}$
and $e^\sharp$ is the obvious map,

Moreover, if $(f, f^\sharp)$ is an equivalence of ringed topoi,
then we can choose the diagram such that
$\mathcal{C}' = \mathcal{D}'$,
$\mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{C}'} = \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{D}'}$

conclusions: There exists i\ge 0 such that f_i:X_i\to Y_i is separated.

theorem.statement: Let \((S_i)_{i\in I}\) be a directed inverse system of schemes with affine transition morphisms and limit \(S=\varprojlim_i S_i\). conclusions: There is an abelian Serre quotient $\mathcal A/\mathcal C$ and an essentially surjective exact quotient functor $F$ with kernel $\mathcal C$.

hypotheses: Let $\mathcal A$ be abelian and $\mathcal C\subset\mathcal A$ a Serre subcategory.
theorem.statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $\mathcal{C} \subset \mathcal{A}$ be a Serre subcategory.
There exists an abelian category $\mathcal{A}/\mathcal{C}$
and an exact functor
$$
F : \mathcal{A} \longrightarrow \mathcal{A}/\mathcal{C}
$$

The category $\mathcal{A}/\mathcal{C}$ and the functor $F$ are
characterized by the following universal property: For any abelian category $\mathcal{B}$ and exact functor $G : \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$ such that
$\mathcal{C} \subset \Ker(G)$ there exists a factorization
$G = H \circ F$ for a unique exact functor
$H : \mathcal{A}/\mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{B}$.

For a finite locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of rank $r$ on $X$, its operational Chern classes are $c_j(\mathcal E)\in A^j(X)$, with $c_0=1$, $c_j=0$ for $j>r$, and total class $c(\mathcal E)=\sum_jc_j(\mathcal E)$. For an integral closed $W\subset X$ of $\delta$-dimension $n$, the classes $c_j(\mathcal E|_W)\cap[W]$ in $\mathrm{CH}_{n-j}(W)$ are characterized via the projective bundle $\pi:\mathbf P(\mathcal E|_W)\to W$ with tautological quotient $\mathcal O(1)$ by $\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i c_1(\mathcal O(1))^i\cap\pi^*c_{r-i}=0$ with $c_0=[W]$. Extend to general cycles by sum and proper pushforward, then to Chow groups.

For a locally free $\mathcal E$ with formal Chern roots $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ (elementary symmetric polynomials equal to $c_i(\mathcal E)$), put $P_p(\mathcal E)=\sum_{j=1}^r x_j^p$, where $P_0=r$, and $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E)=\sum_{p\geq0}P_p(\mathcal E)/p!$. Each $P_p$ is the universal Newton polynomial in the Chern classes, and the degree-$p$ Chern character lies in $A^p(X)\otimes\mathbf Q$.

The derived category $D(\mathcal O_X)$ is the localization of complexes of $\mathcal O_X$-modules at quasi-isomorphisms. A perfect object is locally quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite locally free modules. A locally bounded complex is bounded in cohomological degrees locally on $X$; derived pullback is denoted $Lf^*$ and derived tensor product $\otimes^{\mathbf L}$.

For a bounded complex of finite locally free $\mathcal E^\bullet$, put $c(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\prod_n c(\mathcal E^n)^{(-1)^n}$ (formal multiplication and inversion in $\prod_{p\ge0}A^p(X)$), $P_p(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\sum_n(-1)^n P_p(\mathcal E^n)$ and $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\sum_n(-1)^n\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E^n)$. For a locally bounded complex use this construction on open-and-closed pieces where the terms have constant rank and finitely many are nonzero. When the Chern classes of a perfect object $E$ are defined, these are the unique classes whose pullbacks to a suitable envelope agree with such a representing complex.

An envelope $f:Y\to X$ is a proper morphism such that every $x\in X$ has a preimage $y$ with $\kappa(y)\cong\kappa(x)$. We say Chern classes of a perfect object $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ are defined if an envelope $f:Y\to X$ exists such that $Lf^*E$ is represented by a locally bounded complex of finite locally free sheaves on $Y$.

Under the stated base assumptions, let $X$ be locally of finite type over $S$.

theorem.title: Lemma — Closure

conclusions: If K⊗^L_O (O/I) is bounded above, then the reductions K⊗^L_O(O/I^n) are **uniformly** bounded above for all n≥1.
If the reduction K⊗^L_O(O/I), as an object of D(O/I), has Tor-amplitude [a,b], then for every n≥1 the reduction K⊗^L_O(O/I^n), considered in D(O/I^n), has the same Tor-amplitude [a,b].
hypotheses: (C,O) is a ringed site, I⊂O is a sheaf of ideals and K∈D(O).
theorem.statement:
For a ringed site (C,O), an object E∈D(O) has **Tor-amplitude in [a,b]** (integers a≤b) if H^i(E⊗^L_O F)=0 for every O-module F and every i outside [a,b]. Finite Tor dimension means such a bounded interval exists; **locally** finite Tor dimension means each object has a cover on which a finite interval exists (the interval may vary). An O-module F has Tor dimension ≤d when F[0] has Tor-amplitude in [−d,0] (source Definition tor-amplitude lines 12376–12394). Let I⊂O be a **sheaf of ideals**; derived tensor reduction modulo I^n produces a complex in D(O/I^n). Uniformly bounded above means there exists one upper cohomological bound valid for **all positive n**. The second clause must distinguish Tor-amplitude as an O/I^n-module from Tor-amplitude over O.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}$ be a sheaf of ideals.
Let $K$ be an object of $D(\mathcal{O})$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $K \otimes_\mathcal{O}^\mathbf{L} \mathcal{O}/\mathcal{I}$
is bounded above, then
$K \otimes_\mathcal{O}^\mathbf{L} \mathcal{O}/\mathcal{I}^n$
is uniformly bounded above for all $n$.
\item If $K \otimes_\mathcal{O}^\mathbf{L} \mathcal{O}/\mathcal{I}$
as an object of $D(\mathcal{O}/\mathcal{I})$ has tor amplitude in $[a, b]$,
then $K \otimes_\mathcal{O}^\mathbf{L} \mathcal{O}/\mathcal{I}^n$
as an object of $D(\mathcal{O}/\mathcal{I}^n)$
has tor amplitude in $[a, b]$ for all $n$.
\end{enumerate}

theorem.title: Lemma — Extensions of relative ringed spaces

conclusions: $Y$ is w-local: it is spectral, its closed-point subset is closed, and each point specializes to exactly one closed point.

theorem.statement:
For a topological space $Z$, $\pi_0(Z)$ is its space of connected components. A spectral space is **w-local** when its closed-point subset $Z_0$ is closed and every point specializes to a unique closed point; a continuous map between w-local spaces is **w-local** if it is spectral and sends closed points to closed points. This is terminology, not an additional ambient hypothesis.

Let $X$ be a spectral space such that its set of closed points $X_0$ is closed and each $x\in X$ specializes to a unique closed point. If $Y$ is a closed subspace of $X$, then $Y$ is spectral, its set of closed points is closed in $Y$, and every point of $Y$ specializes to a unique closed point; equivalently, $Y$ is w-local.

theorem.statement: A family $\{f_i:X_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ of schemes is a *universal effective epimorphism* (in a specified category of schemes or affine schemes) if, after every base change $Y\to X$ in that category, the induced family $\{X_i\times_XY\to Y\}$ is an effective epimorphism, meaning that for every test object $T$ the sequence $\operatorname{Hom}(Y,T)\to\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(X_i\times_XY,T)\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}\operatorname{Hom}(X_i\times_X X_j\times_XY,T)$ is an equalizer. If $\{T_i\to T\}$ is an fpqc covering of a scheme $T$, then it is a universal effective epimorphism in the category of schemes. Equivalently, for every base change $T'\to T$ and every test scheme $Z$, every family of maps $h_i:T_i\times_TT'\to Z$ whose restrictions agree on all pairwise fibre products $(T_i\times_TT')\times_{T'}(T_j\times_TT')$ comes from a unique map $h:T'\to Z$. Thus every representable presheaf $\operatorname{Hom}(-,Z)$ on schemes satisfies fpqc descent.

theorem.title: Lemma — Components locally finite

conclusions:
any decent algebraic
space locally of finite type over $X$ is universally catenary.
hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

An algebraic space $X$ is decent if every point $x\in|X|$ admits a quasi-compact representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is reasonable if every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has universally bounded finite fibres, and very reasonable if it is Zariski-locally covered by quasi-compact surjective étale schemes. A morphism $f:X\to Y$ is *decent* (respectively reasonable, very reasonable or with property $(\beta)$) if $X\times_YT$ has that property for every scheme $T\to Y$. Property $(\beta)$ for a space means that every point can be represented by a monomorphism from a field spectrum.

For decent $X$ and $x\in|X|$, $\kappa(x)$ is the field associated with the representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. An *elementary étale neighborhood* $(U,u)\to(X,x)$ is an étale scheme chart whose pointed field map $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to X$ is such a monomorphism. Its henselian local ring is $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{h}=\varinjlim_{(U,u)}\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ over the cofiltered category of elementary étale neighborhoods, and it agrees with $\mathcal O_{U,u}^h$ for any one of them. A decent space's point-set $|X|$ is sober and admits a dense open schematic locus when it has finitely many irreducible components.

theorem.title: Theorem — Cech ss

conclusions: Dualizing complex condition ascends and descends under these covers.
hypotheses: f surjective locally Noetherian, syntomic or flat lci or finite-type Gorenstein; K in D_QCoh(Y).
theorem.statement: For a locally Noetherian scheme $T$, *Cohen–Macaulay* means that every local ring $\mathcal O_{T,t}$ has depth equal to Krull dimension. A complex $D_T\in D(\mathcal O_T)$ is *dualizing* if affine locally it is represented by a bounded coherent complex of finite injective dimension with the self-duality isomorphism $A\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_A(D,D)$. For a flat finite-presentation morphism $f:X\to Y$, *Cohen–Macaulay at $x$* means the local ring of the fibre $X_{f(x)}$ at $x$ is Cohen–Macaulay. A *Gorenstein local ring* is a Noetherian local ring of finite injective dimension as a module over itself; a scheme $T$ is *Gorenstein* if it is locally Noetherian and all its local rings are Gorenstein. A complex in $D(\mathcal O_T)$ is *derived-invertible* if it has a two-sided derived tensor inverse, equivalently it is locally a shift of a line bundle. For a scheme morphism $f:X\to Y$ whose fibres are locally Noetherian, *Gorenstein at $x$* means that $f$ is flat at $x$ and the local ring of $X_{f(x)}$ at $x$ is Gorenstein; *Gorenstein morphism* means this condition at every point. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a surjective morphism of locally Noetherian schemes satisfying at least one of: (i) $f$ syntomic (flat lfp lci); (ii) $f$ flat and a local complete intersection; (iii) $f$ a finite-type Gorenstein morphism (flat with Gorenstein fibres). For any $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$, the complex $K$ is dualizing on $Y$ iff its derived pullback $Lf^*K$ is dualizing on $X$. The assertion includes both ascent and descent; no properness of $f$ is imposed.

Let $a_f$ be the right adjoint to $Rf_*$ on unbounded derived categories with quasi-coherent cohomology, and define the *relative dualizing complex* $\omega_{X/Y}^{\bullet}=a_f(\mathcal O_Y)\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$. Write $X\times_YX$ for the fibre square, $\operatorname{pr}_1,\operatorname{pr}_2:X\times_YX\to X$ for its two projections, and $\Delta:X\to X\times_YX$ for the diagonal. Let $c:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{X\times_YX})\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ be the right adjoint to $R\Delta_*$. Then there are canonical isomorphisms in $D(\mathcal O_X)$:
\[
\mathcal O_X\xrightarrow{\sim}c(L\operatorname{pr}_1^*\omega_{X/Y}^{\bullet})
\quad\text{and}\quad
\mathcal O_X\xrightarrow{\sim}c(L\operatorname{pr}_2^*\omega_{X/Y}^{\bullet}),
\]
and
\[
\omega_{X/Y}^{\bullet}\xrightarrow{\sim}
c(L\operatorname{pr}_1^*\omega_{X/Y}^{\bullet}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X\times_YX}}^{\mathbf L}L\operatorname{pr}_2^*\omega_{X/Y}^{\bullet}).
\]
The statement uses the right adjoint for the *diagonal*, not for $f$ itself, and the two projections are taken on the fibre product.

theorem.title: Lemma — Van den bergh

conclusions: $M$ is flat if and only if every finite relation in $M$ is trivial in the explicitly stated coefficient-matrix sense.
hypotheses: $R$ is a ring and $M$ an $R$-module.
theorem.statement:
A module $M$ over $R$ is flat if and only if
every relation in $M$ is trivial.
Every relation is trivial means: for every $n\geq0$, $f_1,\ldots,f_n\in R$ and $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in M$ with $\sum_i f_i x_i=0$, there exist $m\geq0$, $y_1,\ldots,y_m\in M$ and $a_{ij}\in R$ such that $x_i=\sum_j a_{ij}y_j$ for every $i$ and $\sum_i f_i a_{ij}=0$ for every $j$.

theorem.statement:
Let $R\to S$ be a ring map, $M$ an $S$-module, and $(R,\mathfrak m)$ a complete Noetherian local ring. Assume $S$ is Noetherian and $M$ is finite as an $S$-module. theorem.title: Lemma — Fitting ideal well defined

conclusions: The six conditions listed in the source—strictness, the coimage/image isomorphism, its graded isomorphism, exactness at the middle of each of two graded sequences, and exactness of their combined five-term sequence—are equivalent.
hypotheses: Let $f:A\to B$ be a morphism of finite filtered objects of an abelian category.
theorem.statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $f : A \to B$ be a morphism of finite
filtered objects of $\mathcal{A}$. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is strict,
\item the morphism $\Coim(f) \to \Im(f)$ is an isomorphism,
\item $\text{gr}(\Coim(f)) \to \text{gr}(\Im(f))$ is an
isomorphism,
\item the sequence
$\text{gr}(\Ker(f)) \to \text{gr}(A) \to \text{gr}(B)$
is exact,
\item the sequence $\text{gr}(A) \to \text{gr}(B) \to
\text{gr}(\Coker(f))$ is exact, and
\item the sequence
$$
0 \to
\text{gr}(\Ker(f)) \to
\text{gr}(A) \to
\text{gr}(B) \to
\text{gr}(\Coker(f)) \to 0
$$
is exact.
\end{enumerate}

theorem.title: Lemma — Descend flat finite presentation

conclusions: The stated sequence beginning $0\to f_*\mathcal F\to a_*(\mathcal F|_U)\oplus b_*(\mathcal F|_V)\to c_*(\mathcal F|_{U\cap V})\to R^1f_*\mathcal F\to\cdots$ is long exact and functorial in $\mathcal F$.

Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of ringed spaces.

0 \to

This long exact sequence is functorial in $\mathcal{F}$.

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The derived category $D(\mathcal O_X)$ is the localization of complexes of $\mathcal O_X$-modules at quasi-isomorphisms. A locally bounded complex is bounded in cohomological degrees locally on $X$; derived pullback is denoted $Lf^*$ and derived tensor product $\otimes^{\mathbf L}$.

For a bounded complex of finite locally free $\mathcal E^\bullet$, put $c(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\prod_n c(\mathcal E^n)^{(-1)^n}$ (formal multiplication and inversion in $\prod_{p\ge0}A^p(X)$), $P_p(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\sum_n(-1)^n P_p(\mathcal E^n)$ and $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\sum_n(-1)^n\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E^n)$. When the Chern classes of a perfect object $E$ are defined, these are the unique classes whose pullbacks to a suitable envelope agree with such a representing complex.

We say Chern classes of a perfect object $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ are defined if an envelope $f:Y\to X$ exists such that $Lf^*E$ is represented by a locally bounded complex of finite locally free sheaves on $Y$.

theorem.statement:
For an inverse system of complexes $(K_n)$ in $D(\mathcal O)$, $R\varprojlim K_n$ is its homotopy/derived inverse limit. The $R^1\varprojlim$ terms are first right-derived inverse limits of systems of abelian groups, and the natural comparison to the termwise inverse limit need not be an isomorphism without additional hypotheses. The canonical map $E\to R\varprojlim_n\tau_{\ge -n}E$ uses good truncations. For an inverse system $(K_n)$ of derived objects, write $\mathcal H^m(R\varprojlim K_n)$ for the $m$th cohomology **sheaf** of its homotopy limit. Its evaluation on $V$ is different in general from $H^m(V,R\varprojlim K_n)$; the conclusion is injectivity on sections of cohomology **sheaves**. The function $n(V)$ is an integer depending only on $V$, and $\mathrm{Cov}_V$ is a cofinal system of coverings of $V$.

inverse system in $D(\mathcal{O})$. Let $V \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$
and $m \in \mathbf{Z}$. Assume there exist an integer $n(V)$
and a cofinal system $\text{Cov}_V$ of coverings of $V$ such that
for $\{V_i \to V\} \in \text{Cov}_V$
\begin{enumerate}
\item $R^1\lim H^{m - 1}(V_i, K_n) = 0$, and
\item $H^m(V_i, K_n) \to H^m(V_i, K_{n(V)})$ is injective
for $n \geq n(V)$.
\end{enumerate}
Then the map on sections $H^m(R\lim K_n)(V) \to H^m(K_{n(V)})(V)$ is injective.

conclusions: If $i$ and $j$ are regular immersions, so is $j \circ i$.

theorem.statement:
For functions $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ on a ringed space, regular means successive multiplication maps on $\mathcal O/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})$ are injective; no nonzero-final-quotient condition is imposed here. Koszul-regular means the Koszul complex has zero homology in every positive degree; $H_1$-regular means its degree-one homology vanishes; quasi-regular means, with $\mathcal J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ the ideal sheaf generated by the sequence, that $(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal J^n/\mathcal J^{n+1}$ is an isomorphism, sending $T_i$ to $f_i$ modulo $\mathcal J^2$. An ideal sheaf is of a given type if near each point of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)$ it admits generators of that type. For a ring regular sequence one additionally requires the final quotient nonzero. An immersion is of a given type when its defining ideal on an open where it is closed is of that type. \item If $i$ and $j$ are regular immersions, so is $j \circ i$.
\item If $i$ and $j$ are Koszul-regular immersions, so is $j \circ i$.
\item If $i$ and $j$ are $H_1$-regular immersions, so is $j \circ i$.
\item If $i$ is an $H_1$-regular immersion and $j$ is a quasi-regular
immersion, then $j \circ i$ is a quasi-regular immersion.
\end{enumerate}

theorem.title: Lemma — Geometrically irreducible function field

conclusions: Any locally Noetherian decent algebraic space is quasi-separated.
hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

For $x\in|X|$, condition $(\alpha)_x$ means every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has only finitely many points over $x$. Condition $(\beta)_x$ means there is a monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$. Condition $(\gamma)_x$ means there is a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$, equivalently for every affine étale $U\to X$ both fibres over $x$ of $|U|\to|X|$ and $|U\times_XU|\to|X|$ are finite. The conditions $(\alpha),(\beta),(\gamma)$ mean the corresponding pointwise property holds at every $x$.

An algebraic space $X$ is *decent* when it satisfies $(\gamma)$, equivalently every point $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is *reasonable* when it satisfies $(\delta)$, equivalently the fibres of every affine étale presentation $U\to X$ are universally bounded. It is *very reasonable* when it satisfies $(\epsilon)$, equivalently it has a Zariski-local quasi-compact surjective étale cover by schemes. theorem.title: Proposition — Topological invariance

conclusions:

A \ar[r] \ar[u] & C \ar[u]
}

\begin{enumerate}
\item $A \to C$ is faithfully flat and ind-\'etale,
\item $B \to D$ is faithfully flat and ind-\'etale,
\item $\Spec(C)$ is w-local,
\item $\Spec(D)$ is w-local,
\item $\Spec(D) \to \Spec(C)$ is w-local,
\item the set of closed points of $\Spec(D)$ is the inverse image
of the set of closed points of $\Spec(C)$,
\item the set of closed points of $\Spec(C)$ surjects onto $\Spec(A)$,
\item the set of closed points of $\Spec(D)$ surjects onto $\Spec(B)$,
\item for $\mathfrak m \subset C$ maximal the local ring
$C_\mathfrak m$ is strictly henselian.
\end{enumerate}

conclusions: If $R$ is not Jacobson, there exist a prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$ and $f\in R$ such that $\mathfrak p$ is not maximal, $f\notin\mathfrak p$, $V(\mathfrak p)\cap D(f)=\{\mathfrak p\}$, and $(R/\mathfrak p)_f$ is a field.

hypotheses: $R$ is a commutative ring with identity.
theorem.statement:
Let $R$ be a ring. If $R$ is not Jacobson there exist
a prime $\mathfrak p \subset R$, an element $f \in R$
such that the following hold
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathfrak p$ is not a maximal ideal,
\item $f \not \in \mathfrak p$,
\item $V(\mathfrak p) \cap D(f) = \{\mathfrak p\}$, and
\item $(R/\mathfrak p)_f$ is a field.
\end{enumerate}
On the other hand, if $R$ is Jacobson, then for any pair $(\mathfrak p, f)$
such that (1) and (2) hold the set $V(\mathfrak p) \cap D(f)$ is
infinite.

finite surjective morphism $X' \to X$ of finite presentation such that
$\xi$ pulls back to zero in $H^q_\etale(X' \times_X Z, \underline{M})$.

Let $B\to A$ and $A'\to A$ be ring homomorphisms with $A'\to A$ surjective and kernel $I$. Put $B'=B\times_A A'$.

theorem.title: Lemma — Affineline special

conclusions: Gorenstein iff dualizing complex invertible, with local and open-locus claims and O_X normalization.
hypotheses: X locally Noetherian; dualizing D_X for part 1, X Gorenstein for part 2.
theorem.statement: A *Gorenstein local ring* is a Noetherian local ring of finite injective dimension as a module over itself; a scheme $T$ is *Gorenstein* if it is locally Noetherian and all its local rings are Gorenstein. A complex in $D(\mathcal O_T)$ is *derived-invertible* if it has a two-sided derived tensor inverse, equivalently it is locally a shift of a line bundle. For a scheme morphism $f:X\to Y$ whose fibres are locally Noetherian, *Gorenstein at $x$* means that $f$ is flat at $x$ and the local ring of $X_{f(x)}$ at $x$ is Gorenstein; *Gorenstein morphism* means this condition at every point. Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme. (1) If $D_X$ is any dualizing complex on $X$, then (a) $X$ is Gorenstein iff $D_X$ is derived-invertible on $X$; (b) for every $x\in X$, the ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is Gorenstein iff its derived stalk $(D_X)_x$ is an invertible object of $D(\mathcal O_{X,x})$; and (c) the locus of Gorenstein points is an open Gorenstein subscheme. (2) If $X$ is Gorenstein, then the existence of *some* dualizing complex on $X$ is equivalent to the structure complex $\mathcal O_X[0]$ itself being dualizing. The equivalences refer to derived-invertibility, not mere invertibility of a chosen cohomology sheaf unless the complex is concentrated in one degree.

theorem.title: Proposition — Locally quasi separated open dense scheme

conclusions: Four precise composition and descent implications for Gorenstein morphisms.
hypotheses: Three locally Noetherian fibre systems; additional flatness of f for converse directions.
theorem.statement: A *Gorenstein local ring* is a Noetherian local ring of finite injective dimension as a module over itself; a scheme $T$ is *Gorenstein* if it is locally Noetherian and all its local rings are Gorenstein. A complex in $D(\mathcal O_T)$ is *derived-invertible* if it has a two-sided derived tensor inverse, equivalently it is locally a shift of a line bundle. For a scheme morphism $f:X\to Y$ whose fibres are locally Noetherian, *Gorenstein at $x$* means that $f$ is flat at $x$ and the local ring of $X_{f(x)}$ at $x$ is Gorenstein; *Gorenstein morphism* means this condition at every point. Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$ be morphisms such that *all* fibres of $f,g,g\circ f$ are locally Noetherian. Then (1) if $f$ is Gorenstein at $x$ and $g$ at $f(x)$, $g\circ f$ is Gorenstein at $x$; (2) if $f$ and $g$ are Gorenstein everywhere, then $g\circ f$ is Gorenstein; (3) if $g\circ f$ is Gorenstein at $x$ and $f$ is flat at $x$, then $f$ is Gorenstein at $x$ and $g$ at $f(x)$; (4) if $g\circ f$ is Gorenstein everywhere and $f$ flat everywhere, then $f$ is Gorenstein everywhere and $g$ is Gorenstein **at points in the image of $f$**, not necessarily outside that image.

theorem.title: Lemma — Base change representable

conclusions: The stated assignments define a functorial cosimplicial $(A/R)_\bullet$-module.
hypotheses: $R\to A$ is a commutative-ring map and $(N,\varphi)$ a module descent datum satisfying the cocycle identity.
theorem.statement:
Let $R\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings. An $A$-module descent datum is an $A$-module $N$ together with an isomorphism of $A\otimes_R A$-modules $\varphi:N\otimes_R A\xrightarrow{\sim}A\otimes_R N$ such that the two induced ways of transporting $N$ across three $A$-factors agree (the usual cocycle identity on $A\otimes_R A\otimes_R A$). Set $B_n=A^{\otimes_R(n+1)}$ for $n\geq0$. For $0\leq i\leq n$, define the $B_n$-module $N_{n,i}=A^{\otimes_R i}\otimes_R N\otimes_R A^{\otimes_R(n-i)}$ with $N$ in tensor position $i$. The descent isomorphism supplies compatible $B_n$-linear identifications $\varphi^n_{ij}:N_{n,i}\to N_{n,j}$ for $i\leq j$, and for an order-preserving map $\beta:[n]\to[m]$ there is a canonical $B_n\to B_m$-semilinear map $N_{\beta,n}:N_{n,n}\to N_{m,\beta(n)}$ sending $1\otimes\cdots\otimes n$ to the corresponding tensor in position $\beta(n)$. Define $N_n=N_{n,n}$ and
$$N_\bullet(\beta)=\varphi^m_{\beta(n),m}\circ N_{\beta,n}:N_n\to N_m.$$
Then $(N_n,N_\bullet(\beta))$ is a cosimplicial module over the cosimplicial $R$-algebra $B_\bullet$, and the construction is functorial in $(N,\varphi)$.

\[
K\xrightarrow{\sim}R\operatorname{Hom}_A(R\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,\omega_A^\bullet),\omega_A^\bullet)
\]
is an isomorphism, natural in every $K\in D_{\rm Coh}(A)$, so $\mathbb D_A^2\simeq\mathrm{id}$.

conclusions: Gorensteinness, flatness with Gorenstein fibres, and invertibility of the relative dualizing module (globally/affine locally) are equivalent.

For an affine map of Noetherian rings $A\to B$ arising locally from $f$, define $\omega_{B/A}=\operatorname{Hom}_A(E,A)\otimes_EB$ using a finite $A$-algebra $E$ for which $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}E$ is an open immersion, and let $\omega_{Y/X}$ be the coherent sheaf formed by gluing these modules. hypotheses: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a flat morphism $h:T'\to T$ of relative dimension $r$, the flat pullback $h^*:Z_q(T)\to Z_{q+r}(T')$ sends $[W]$ to the cycle $[T'\times_TW]_{q+r}$ weighted by the lengths at generic points of components. It descends to Chow groups.

For a finite locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of rank $r$ on $X$, its operational Chern classes are $c_j(\mathcal E)\in A^j(X)$, with $c_0=1$, $c_j=0$ for $j>r$, and total class $c(\mathcal E)=\sum_jc_j(\mathcal E)$. theorem.title: Lemma — Flat base change cotangent complex

conclusions:
for every \'etale morphism
$\varphi : U \to X$ from a scheme $U$ and any $u \in U$ with
$\varphi(u) = x$, exists a point $u'\in U$, $u' \leadsto u$ with
$\varphi(u') = x'$.
hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

For $x\in|X|$, condition $(\alpha)_x$ means every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has only finitely many points over $x$. Condition $(\beta)_x$ means there is a monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$. Condition $(\gamma)_x$ means there is a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$, equivalently for every affine étale $U\to X$ both fibres over $x$ of $|U|\to|X|$ and $|U\times_XU|\to|X|$ are finite. The conditions $(\alpha),(\beta),(\gamma)$ mean the corresponding pointwise property holds at every $x$.

An algebraic space $X$ is *decent* when it satisfies $(\gamma)$, equivalently every point $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is *reasonable* when it satisfies $(\delta)$, equivalently the fibres of every affine étale presentation $U\to X$ are universally bounded. It is *very reasonable* when it satisfies $(\epsilon)$, equivalently it has a Zariski-local quasi-compact surjective étale cover by schemes. The implications scheme or quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ very reasonable $\Rightarrow$ reasonable $\Rightarrow$ decent hold.

For $x\in|X|$ and an étale morphism $U\to X$, write $(U,u)\to(X,x)$ for a pointed étale neighborhood. It is *elementary* when $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to X$ is a monomorphism representing $x$. When $X$ is decent, such neighborhoods are cofiltered: they exist, any two have a common refinement and parallel arrows can be equalized after refinement. The residue field $\kappa(x)$ is the field of the unique representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$, and the henselian local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{h}$ is the filtered colimit of $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ over elementary étale neighborhoods; equivalently $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{h}\cong\mathcal O_{U,u}^{h}$ for any elementary étale neighborhood.

For points $a,b$ of a topological space, $b\leadsto a$ means $a\in\overline{\{b\}}$, i.e., $a$ is a specialization of $b$. The space is $T_0$ (Kolmogorov) when distinct points have distinct closures, and sober when every irreducible closed subset has exactly one generic point. A subset is locally constructible if its intersection with every quasi-compact open subset is a finite union of locally closed subsets. An algebraic space has a locally constructible subset in the étale sense when its inverse image in every étale scheme chart is locally constructible.

$\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$
be a standard $\tau$-covering of this site.

\begin{enumerate}
\item $V$ is an affine scheme,
\item $\mathcal{V} = \{V \to U\}$ is an fpqc covering

$\check{\mathcal{C}}^\bullet (\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{F})$ and

conclusions: Finite generation, finite presentation, flatness, faithful flatness, and finite projectivity descend and ascend along $f$.

theorem.statement: A homomorphism $f:R\to S$ of commutative rings is universally injective (or pure as an $R$-module map) if, for every $R$-module $T$, the canonical map $T\to T\otimes_R S$ is injective. The same pure ring map $f$ is used in each assertion.

For a smooth curve it is finite purely inseparable of degree $p^n$ (for $n\ge0$). A morphism of proper integral curves is nonconstant if its function-field homomorphism is injective and not just an extension of constants.

conclusions: If it is cartesian and $k$ epic, it is cocartesian and $f$ epic.

theorem.statement:
For functions $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ on a ringed space, regular means successive multiplication maps on $\mathcal O/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})$ are injective; no nonzero-final-quotient condition is imposed here. Koszul-regular means the Koszul complex has zero homology in every positive degree; $H_1$-regular means its degree-one homology vanishes; quasi-regular means, with $\mathcal J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ the ideal sheaf generated by the sequence, that $(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal J^n/\mathcal J^{n+1}$ is an isomorphism, sending $T_i$ to $f_i$ modulo $\mathcal J^2$. An ideal sheaf is of a given type if near each point of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)$ it admits generators of that type. For a ring regular sequence one additionally requires the final quotient nonzero. An immersion is of a given type when its defining ideal on an open where it is closed is of that type. Relative quasi/$H_1$-regular means also that its source is flat over the base. Let $X$ be a ringed space.

We have the following implications
$f_1, \ldots, f_r$ is a regular sequence $\Rightarrow$
$f_1, \ldots, f_r$ is a Koszul-regular sequence $\Rightarrow$
$f_1, \ldots, f_r$ is an $H_1$-regular sequence $\Rightarrow$
$f_1, \ldots, f_r$ is a quasi-regular sequence.

and the remaining map uniquely determined.

theorem.title: Lemma — Property irreducible

conclusions: a_f preserves supports and localizes on arbitrary opens.
hypotheses: f perfect proper Noetherian; T closed and V open.
theorem.statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a *perfect proper* morphism of Noetherian schemes (proper and of finite Tor-dimension, with the usual pseudo-coherence/finiteness built into perfectness) and let $a_f$ be the right adjoint of $Rf_*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$. A complex in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ is *supported on* a closed subset $T$ if every cohomology sheaf is zero on $Y\setminus T$. If $V\subseteq Y$ is open, $U=f^{-1}(V)$, and $j:V\hookrightarrow Y$, $j':U\hookrightarrow X$, the *restriction comparison* is the natural map $\rho_K:(j')^*a_f(K)\to a_{f|_U}(j^*K)$. Then (1) for every closed $T\subseteq Y$, any $Q\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ supported on $T$ has $a_f(Q)$ supported on $f^{-1}(T)$; and (2) for every open $V\subseteq Y$ and every $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$, the natural restriction map $\rho_K:a_f(K)|_{f^{-1}(V)}\to a_{f|_{f^{-1}(V)}}(K|_V)$ is an isomorphism, understood locally on the open $V$ when it is not quasi-compact.

hypotheses: Quasi-coherent modules on the small étale ringed site of a scheme.
theorem.statement: Let $S$ be a scheme, and let $\operatorname{QCoh}(S_{\mathrm{\acute et}},\mathcal O)$ denote quasi-coherent modules on its small étale ringed site. This category has the following closure properties (where exactness, colimits and internal Hom are taken in the ambient category of site modules): (1) arbitrary direct sums and (2) arbitrary colimits are quasi-coherent; (3) kernels and cokernels of morphisms between quasi-coherent modules are quasi-coherent; (4) in a short exact sequence of site modules, if any two of the three terms are quasi-coherent, so is the third; (5) tensor products of quasi-coherent modules are quasi-coherent; (6) if $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ are quasi-coherent and $\mathcal F$ is of finite presentation, then $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)$ is quasi-coherent.

theorem.statement: For a locally Noetherian scheme $T$, *Cohen–Macaulay* means that every local ring $\mathcal O_{T,t}$ has depth equal to Krull dimension. A complex $D_T\in D(\mathcal O_T)$ is *dualizing* if affine locally it is represented by a bounded coherent complex of finite injective dimension with the self-duality isomorphism $A\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_A(D,D)$. For a flat finite-presentation morphism $f:X\to Y$, *Cohen–Macaulay at $x$* means the local ring of the fibre $X_{f(x)}$ at $x$ is Cohen–Macaulay. Fix a Noetherian scheme $S$ and the category $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ of separated finite-type $S$-schemes. For $f:X\to Y$ therein, let $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ be the upper-shriek functor built from the right adjoint to proper pushforward on a compactification $X\hookrightarrow\bar X\to Y$. In particular $f^!\mathcal O_Y$ is a coherent bounded complex when $f$ is perfect. Let $f:X\to Y$ be flat in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$, and $x\in X$. The following conditions are equivalent: (1) the fibre-local ring $\mathcal O_{X_{f(x)},x}$ is Cohen–Macaulay; (2) there is an open neighbourhood $U\subseteq X$ of $x$ on which $f^!\mathcal O_Y|_U$ is quasi-isomorphic to a *single* coherent cohomology sheaf placed in one cohomological degree (the degree may depend on $U$). In particular this is a neighbourhood statement about the relative dualizing complex, not just its single stalk.

equidimensional of dimension $1$ whose singularities are at-worst-nodal.
If $Y \subset X$ is a reduced closed subscheme

\end{enumerate}

Let $X$ be an algebraic space locally of finite type over a field $k$.
Consider the conditions
